correctness.rationale: The mass-weighted Jacobi operator is a finite-rank perturbation with essential band [0,4] and no square-summable band solutions. For λ=2+2cosh t the exactly evaluated 2×2 Birman–Schwinger eigenvalues F±(t) are strictly decreasing; F+(0+)=∞, F−(0+)=4dab/(a+b), F±(∞)<1. These endpoint inequalities imply exactly one versus two simple above-band eigenvalues and the equality resonance. At fixed s=a+b, F− increases strictly with ab, whose unique maximizer is a=b=s/2. Expansion F−(t)=4dab/s−[4ab d²(a²+b²)/s³]t+O(t²) gives the stated quadratic weak-mode gap and localization length on compact strictly-positive threshold paths. Independently rechecked numerical roots, monotonicity and onset for 24 parameter cases; they corroborate rather than establish the infinite theorem.
residual_risks: Only compact positive threshold paths are covered by the quadratic-onset uniformity; numerical checks do not prove the infinite statement.
